question: The Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) was passed on which date?
detailedExplanation: The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 24th session of the All-India Muslim League in Minto Park (now Iqbal Park), Lahore on 22-24 March 1940, with 23 March 1940 as the key day. It demanded autonomous Muslim states in the north-western and eastern zones of the subcontinent.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Who formally moved the Lahore Resolution in the Muslim League session of 1940?
detailedExplanation: A. K. Fazl-ul-Haq, the Chief Minister of Bengal, moved the Lahore Resolution on 23 March 1940. Quaid-e-Azam presided over the session and delivered his famous speech clarifying that the Muslims were a separate nation.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Who coined the name 'Pakistan' and in which year?
detailedExplanation: Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a student at Cambridge, coined the word 'Pakistan' in his pamphlet 'Now or Never' published in January 1933. The letters stand for Punjab, Afghania (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa), Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The All-India Muslim League was founded in which city in 1906?
detailedExplanation: The All-India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at the annual session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference in Dhaka. Its first president was Sir Aga Khan III, and its first session was held at Karachi in 1907.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Simla Deputation (1906) presented the demand of separate electorates to which Viceroy?
detailedExplanation: A deputation of 35 Muslims led by Sir Aga Khan met Viceroy Lord Minto at Simla on 1 October 1906 and demanded separate electorates for Muslims. This demand was accepted and incorporated in the Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Who is called the founder of the Aligarh Movement?
detailedExplanation: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Aligarh Movement to modernize Muslim education. He established the Scientific Society (1864), the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh (1875), and launched the journal Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq. The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College was established in which year?
detailedExplanation: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the MAO College at Aligarh in 1875. It was upgraded to Aligarh Muslim University in 1920. The college was a cornerstone of the Aligarh Movement that revived modern education among Muslims.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was launched by the Ali brothers mainly to:
optionB: Support the Ottoman Caliphate against the Allied powers
detailedExplanation: After World War I, the Allied powers planned to dismantle the Ottoman Caliphate. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali launched the Khilafat Movement (1919) to protect the Turkish Caliphate, in alliance with the Congress-led non-cooperation movement.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was signed between the Congress and the Muslim League under the leadership of:
optionD: Maulana Azad and Liaquat Ali Khan
detailedExplanation: The Lucknow Pact (December 1916) united the Congress and the Muslim League, which both held their annual sessions in Lucknow. Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Bal Gangadhar Tilak were the chief architects; Jinnah was called the 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity' by Sarojini Naidu.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Jinnah presented his famous Fourteen Points in response to:
detailedExplanation: The Nehru Report (1928), prepared by Motilal Nehru's committee, rejected separate electorates and proposed a unitary constitution. In reply, Quaid-e-Azam drafted his Fourteen Points in March 1929 to safeguard Muslim rights and interests.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Allama Iqbal delivered his famous Allahabad Address (idea of a separate Muslim state) in which year?
detailedExplanation: Allama Iqbal, as president of the All-India Muslim League session at Allahabad, delivered his historic address on 29 December 1930, proposing that the north-western Muslim-majority provinces of India should be formed into an autonomous Muslim state.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The 'Day of Deliverance' (22 December 1939) was observed by the Muslim League to mark:
detailedExplanation: Congress ministries in seven provinces resigned in October-November 1939 over the war issue. The Muslim League declared 22 December 1939 as the 'Day of Deliverance' to express relief at the end of Congress rule, which it claimed had oppressed Muslims.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Cabinet Mission Plan was presented in which year?
detailedExplanation: The Cabinet Mission (Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and Alexander) visited India in March 1946 and presented its plan on 16 May 1946, proposing a three-tier federal structure. The Muslim League accepted it initially but withdrew after the Congress interpretation of the grouping clause.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Direct Action Day was observed by the Muslim League on:
detailedExplanation: After the Cabinet Mission impasse, the Muslim League announced Direct Action for 16 August 1946 to achieve Pakistan through struggle. The day led to violent communal clashes, mainly in Calcutta, accelerating the demand for a separate state.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The 3rd June Plan (1947), which announced the partition of India, was also known as:
detailedExplanation: The Mountbatten Plan announced on 3 June 1947 proposed partition of India into two dominions. It was accepted by the Congress, the Muslim League and the Sikhs. The Indian Independence Act 1947 was later passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The boundary line between India and Pakistan was drawn by the Radcliffe Commission headed by:
detailedExplanation: The Radcliffe Commission, chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, was appointed to demarcate the boundaries of Punjab and Bengal. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947, after independence.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Objectives Resolution, which became the foundation of all Pakistan constitutions, was presented by:
detailedExplanation: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 7 March 1949; it was adopted on 12 March 1949. It declared that sovereignty belongs to Allah and laid down principles for the future constitution.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Constitution of 1956 was promulgated on 23 March 1956. What was its key feature?
optionB: Parliamentary system with Urdu and Bengali as national languages
detailedExplanation: The 1956 Constitution established a parliamentary system under a Prime Minister, a single house of parliament and declared Urdu and Bengali as national languages. It was abrogated by General Ayub Khan on 7 October 1958.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Constitution of 1962 introduced which system of government?
detailedExplanation: The 1962 Constitution, promulgated by President Ayub Khan, introduced a presidential system with an indirectly elected president and the Basic Democracies framework. It was abrogated by General Yahya Khan in March 1969.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Constitution of 1973 was passed by the National Assembly on:
detailedExplanation: The 1973 Constitution was unanimously passed by the National Assembly on 10 April 1973 and came into effect on 14 August 1973. It established a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister as the chief executive.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
detailedExplanation: Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956 when the 1956 Constitution was promulgated. Before that, the head of state was the Governor-General. He was ousted by Ayub Khan in October 1958.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The 18th Amendment (2010) in the Constitution is best known for:
optionB: Abolishing the Concurrent List and devolving subjects to provinces
detailedExplanation: The 18th Amendment, passed unanimously on 8 April 2010, abolished the Concurrent List, devolved many subjects to provinces, renamed NWFP to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and increased provincial autonomy. It is considered the most wide-ranging amendment in Pakistan's history.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The largest province of Pakistan by area is:
detailedExplanation: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area, covering about 44% of the country's total area. Punjab is the most populous province.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Which is the longest river of Pakistan?
detailedExplanation: The Indus is the longest river of Pakistan, flowing about 2,900 km within Pakistan. It originates from Tibet (near Mansarovar) and enters the Arabian Sea near Karachi. The Sutlej is the longest tributary of the Indus.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: According to the Indus Water Treaty (1960), which rivers were allocated to Pakistan?
detailedExplanation: The Indus Water Treaty, signed on 19 September 1960 between India and Pakistan (mediated by the World Bank), gave the western rivers - Indus, Jhelum and Chenab - to Pakistan and the eastern rivers - Ravi, Sutlej and Beas - to India.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Tarbela Dam, the largest dam of Pakistan, is built on which river?
detailedExplanation: Tarbela Dam, completed in 1974, is constructed on the Indus River near Haripur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Mangla Dam is built on the Jhelum River (completed 1967). Diamer-Bhasha Dam is under construction on the Indus.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: K-2, the second highest peak in the world, is situated in which mountain range?
detailedExplanation: K-2 (8,611 m) lies in the Karakoram Range on the Pakistan-China border. It was first climbed in 1954 by an Italian expedition (Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni). Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is the second highest peak of Pakistan.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
detailedExplanation: The Khyber Pass, in the Safed Koh range, connects Peshawar (Pakistan) with Jalalabad and Kabul (Afghanistan). The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with China through the Karakoram Highway.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The largest desert of Pakistan is:
detailedExplanation: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is the largest desert of Pakistan and lies mostly in Sindh. Cholistan is in Punjab (Bahawalpur), Thal is spread over Mianwali and nearby districts, and Kharan lies in Balochistan.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Which is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan?
detailedExplanation: Manchar Lake, in Jamshoro district of Sindh, is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan. Keenjhar Lake in Sindh is the second largest. Saif-ul-Malook lies in Kaghan Valley, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The national animal of Pakistan is:
detailedExplanation: The Markhor (a wild goat) is the national animal of Pakistan. The Chukar partridge is the national bird, Deodar is the national tree, Jasmine is the national flower and Mango is the national fruit. Hockey is the national sport.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The white portion in the flag of Pakistan represents:
detailedExplanation: The flag of Pakistan has a dark green field with a white crescent and star, and a vertical white stripe at the hoist. The white portion represents the minorities of Pakistan. The flag was designed by Amir-ud-Din Qadwai and adopted on 11 August 1947.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The national anthem of Pakistan was written by:
detailedExplanation: The national anthem 'Qaumi Tarana' was written by Hafeez Jalandhari in 1952, composed by Ahmed G. Chagla, and officially adopted on 13 August 1954. It was first played on the radio the same day.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Minar-e-Pakistan, built at the site of the Lahore Resolution, is located in:
detailedExplanation: Minar-e-Pakistan stands in Iqbal Park (formerly Minto Park), Lahore, where the Lahore Resolution was passed on 23 March 1940. It was designed by architect Nasreddin Murat-Khan and completed in 1968.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 in which city?
detailedExplanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi. He was educated at Bombay and London, enrolled at Lincoln's Inn in 1896, and rose to be one of the greatest constitutional lawyers of the subcontinent.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Quaid-e-Azam served as the first Governor-General of Pakistan for how long?
optionB: About one year and two months
detailedExplanation: Jinnah became the first Governor-General of Pakistan on 14 August 1947 and served until his death on 11 September 1948 - about one year and two months. He was also the first President of the Constituent Assembly.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Allama Iqbal was born in which city of Punjab?
detailedExplanation: Allama Muhammad Iqbal was born on 9 November 1877 in Sialkot. He studied at Government College Lahore and later at Cambridge and Munich. His famous works include Asrar-e-Khudi, Payam-e-Mashriq, Bang-e-Dara and Zarb-e-Kaleem.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
detailedExplanation: Liaquat Ali Khan served as the first Prime Minister of Pakistan from 14 August 1947 until his assassination on 16 October 1951 in Rawalpindi. He is also called 'Quaid-e-Millat'.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The 1965 war between Pakistan and India lasted for how many days?
detailedExplanation: The 1965 war began on 6 September 1965, when India attacked Pakistan across the international border, and ended on 23 September 1965 under a UN-brokered ceasefire - a total of 17 days. The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Tashkent Declaration of January 1966 was signed between:
optionD: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
detailedExplanation: After the 1965 war, President Ayub Khan and Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri signed the Tashkent Declaration on 10 January 1966, mediated by the Soviet Union. Both countries agreed to withdraw to pre-war positions.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: East Pakistan separated to form Bangladesh in which year?
detailedExplanation: Following the political crisis of 1971 and the December 1971 war with India, East Pakistan became the independent state of Bangladesh. The Instrument of Surrender was signed in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 (Yahya Khan era).
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Simla Agreement (1972) was signed between:
detailedExplanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972, after the 1971 war. Both countries agreed to resolve issues bilaterally and respect the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Pakistan conducted its first successful nuclear tests (Chagai-I) on:
detailedExplanation: Pakistan carried out five nuclear tests at Ras Koh Hills, Chagai, Balochistan on 28 May 1998, followed by a sixth test in the Kharan desert on 30 May 1998. The nuclear programme was initiated by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in 1972.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission was headed by which scientist when the Chagai tests were conducted?
detailedExplanation: Dr. Munir Ahmad Khan was the Chairman of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC) during the 1998 tests. Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan headed the Kahuta Research Laboratories (KRL), established in 1976.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a flagship project of which initiative?
detailedExplanation: CPEC, launched in 2015, is a flagship project of China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). It connects Gwadar Port in Pakistan with Kashgar in China through road, rail and energy projects, and is also known as 'One Belt, One Road'.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Gwadar Port, the deep-sea port of Pakistan, is located in which province?
detailedExplanation: Gwadar Port is located on the Makran coast of Balochistan, overlooking the Arabian Sea and the Strait of Hormuz. It is operated under CPEC and is Pakistan's third major port after Karachi and Port Qasim.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The State Bank of Pakistan was established in which year?
detailedExplanation: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) was established on 1 July 1948 under the State Bank of Pakistan Act 1956 (originally set up in 1948). Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated it, and it remained the issuer of currency from 1 April 1949.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Which sector contributes the largest share to Pakistan's exports?
detailedExplanation: Textile and garments are the largest export sector of Pakistan, contributing more than half of the country's total exports. Cotton and textile-related industries also employ a large share of the industrial workforce.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Nishan-e-Haider, the highest military award of Pakistan, is awarded for:
detailedExplanation: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award of Pakistan, given for exceptional valour in battle. So far it has been awarded to ten recipients, including Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar, Major Aziz Bhatti, Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas and Captain Karnal Sher Khan.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
detailedExplanation: General Sir Frank Messervy was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army (1947-48). General Muhammad Ayub Khan became the first native Pakistani C-in-C in 1951. The country's first COAS after 1972 restructuring was General Tikka Khan.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is located in:
detailedExplanation: The Pakistan Navy's Headquarters (NHQ) is in Karachi. The Navy was created on 14 August 1947 with the Royal Pakistan Navy's ships transferred from the British Royal Indian Navy.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The National Assembly of Pakistan, after the 26th Constitutional Amendment (2024), has how many total seats?
detailedExplanation: The 26th Constitutional Amendment, passed in October 2024, reduced the National Assembly's total seats from 342 to 336. The amendment also introduced constitutional benches in the Supreme Court and changed the process of appointing the Chief Justice.
subject: pakistan-affairs

question: The Pakistan Super League (PSL) 2026 - its eleventh season - began on which date?
detailedExplanation: PSL Season 11 (2026) started on 26 March 2026. The PSL began in 2016 with Islamabad United winning the inaugural title; Lahore Qalandars won back-to-back titles in 2022 and 2023.
subject: current-affairs

question: Pakistan held its 5G spectrum auction on 10 March 2026, raising approximately how much revenue?
detailedExplanation: Pakistan's first 5G spectrum auction, held on 10 March 2026, raised approximately US$507 million. The auction marked the commercial rollout of 5G services in Pakistan after years of preparation by the telecom regulator.
subject: current-affairs

question: Which four countries participated in the Islamabad quadrilateral diplomatic meeting of 29-30 March 2026?
detailedExplanation: Pakistan hosted a quadrilateral diplomatic meeting on 29-30 March 2026 with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Egypt. The meeting was aimed at consolidating regional backing for de-escalation and preparing for talks between the United States and Iran.
subject: current-affairs
